slides.title: THE DEMONSTRATIVES 	PRONOUNS

paragraphs.text: ITO, IYAN & IYON

slides.title: l. The demonstrative ito ( this )

paragraphs.text: The demonstrative Ito (pronounced i -to) is used to refer to a thing that is very near or close to the person speaking. It is followed by the linking verb ay in a subject-predicate sentence word order. The linking verb ay may be shortened to 'y as it follows the word ito . ln an inverted word order sentence where the predicate comes at the beginning, such as the sentence “ maliit ito ,” the linking verb ay is dropped.

slides.title: Example: This is John. lto'y si John.

paragraphs.text: This is a child. lto'y bata.
This is food. Ito’y pagkain .
This is small. Maliit ito
This is big. 				Malaki ito .

slides.title: 2. THE DEMONSTRATIVE IYAN (THAT)

paragraphs.text: The demonstrative iyan (pronounced l-YAN) is used to refer to a thing that is near the person spo­ken to. It is followed by ay .
Example:
That is Mary. lyan ay si Mary.
That is food. lyan ay pagkain .
That is Mary's food.			 Iyan ay pagkain ni Mary.
That is plenty.				   	 Marami iyan .
That is hot. Mainit iyan .

slides.title: 3.	THE DEMONSTRATIVE IYON ( THAT, OVER THERE )

paragraphs.text: The demonstrative iyon (pronounced I-YON) is used to refer to a thing that is far from both the per­son speaking and the one spoken to.
Example:
That is Pasig River. lyon ay llog Pasig.
That is long. lyon ay mahaba .
That is clean and long. lyon ay malinis at mahaba .
That is clean.								Malinis iyon .
That is long. Mahaba iyon

slides.title: 4.PLURAL FORMS ITO , IYAN AND IYON

paragraphs.text: Note that since Tagalog sentences follow a plurality rule and either or both the subject or predicate may be made plural, sentences containing the plural forms of ito , iyan , and iyon may be marked by the plural marker ang mga . The singular forms of ito , iyan , and iyon are not preceded by ang ; but the plural forms of these words are preceded by the plural article ang mga . This and that thus become these and those. These are good.				Ang mga ito ay mababait .
Those are big.					Ang mga iyan ay malalaki .
Those are clean.				Ang mga iyon ay malilinis .

slides.title: THIS AND THAT AS MODIFIERS

paragraphs.text: The demonstratives ito , iyan , and iyon can also be used as modifiers to point out or specify the sub­ject of a sentence. It is interesting to note that when used as modifiers, these demonstratives are placed before the noun and may also be repeated for emphasis before the linking verb ay in a subject-predicate sentence (see first example) or are the end of an inverted word order sentence (see second exam­ple below). Either sentence structure is acceptable but the first one is more formal and the second is more colloquial.

slides.title: Ang mesa ng ito ay malinis .				This table is clean.

paragraphs.text: lto ng mesa ng ito ay malinis .
Malaki ang bahay na iyon . 				That house is big.
Malaki iyon g bahay na iyon .
Maganda ang suot mo ng iyan . 			Your clothes are beautiful.
Maganda iyan g suot mo ng iyan .
Observe the use of - ng, -g and na in the following phrases:
ito ng mesa ng ito
iyan g suot mo ng iyan
iyon g bahay na iyon

slides.title: In these phrase, the connective - ng is attached to the modifier ito , the noun mesa, and the pronoun mo ; the connective -g is attached to the modifiers iyan and iyon ; and the connective na comes after the noun bahay .

paragraphs.text: The purpose of these three connectives or ligature , to be discussed in the next lesson is to connect the ff:
a demonstrative and a noun ( itong mesa, iyang suot , iyong bahay )
a noun and a demonstrative ( bahay na iyon , mesang ito )
a possessive pronoun and a demonstrative ( mong iyan )

In a sentence containing the demonstratives ito , iyan , and iyon and the marker sa (which means in, at, on or to, and is used to denote the location of an action), the demonstratives ito , iyan , or iyon always appear after the noun at the end of the sentence.
Ang bata ay kumain sa mesa ng ito .   		The child ate on this table.
Pumunta kami sa bahay na iyan .			We went to that house.
Sumakay sila sa bus na iyon .				They rode on that bus.

slides.title: Exercises

paragraphs.text: You are in front of the class behind the teacher's desk pointing out where things are in the classroom. Show where the following things are by filling in the blanks below with the proper singular or plural forms of the demonstratives ito , iyan , or iyon .
1.______________ ang aking lamesa . (table)
2.(Pointing to a student's seat)___________ ay upuan ng estudyante .
3.Sa likod (at the back) ay ang malaking pisara (blackboard). __________ay susulatan ko ng mga takdang-aralin ( homeworks ).
4.Sa kanan (to the right) ay mga libro . ______________	ay babasahin natin.
5.Sa kaliwa (to your left) ninyo ay mga bintana . __________	ay palaging nakabukas .
(always open)

slides.title: WORDS THAT LINK AND DESCRIBE

A peculiar but noteworthy feature of the Tagalog language is the use of connectives or ligatures to "link together " two adjacent words . The ligature suffixes - ng and -g are attached to the end of the first word in a sequence whereas the ligature word na is placed between the two words .

paragraphs.text: These ligatures have no particular meaning of their own, but merely indicate that there is a close rela­tionship between the two words and that, generally, one modifies the other.

slides.title: 1.The suffix ligature - NG

paragraphs.text: The ligature - ng is attached as a suffix to the end of words that end in vowels. a,e , i o,u
Ang malaki ng bahay ay isang paaralan .   		( malaki + -ng + bahay )
The big house is a school.				big house
Marunong ang bata ng mabait .				(bata + -ng + mabait )
The good child is intelligent.				good child
I. THE RULES FOR USING EACH TYPE OF LIGATURE

slides.title: 2. The suffix ligature - G

paragraphs.text: The ligature -g is attached as a suffix to the end of words that end in the consonant N.
Ang mayaman g lalaki ay mapagbigay .		( mayaman + -g + lalaki )
The rich man is generous. rich man
I. THE RULES FOR USING EACH TYPE OF LIGATURE

slides.title: 3.The ligature NA

paragraphs.text: The ligature word na is used after words that end in consonants other than n.
Kumain siya ng maasim na mangga . 		( maasim + na + mangga )
He/She ate a sour mango .			Sour mango
mangga ng maasim
I. THE RULES FOR USING EACH TYPE OF LIGATURE

slides.title: Maganda ang tahimik na bata. ( tahimik + na + bata)

paragraphs.text: The quiet child is beautiful.			quiet child
Note that the above sequences are made up of adjective + noun or noun + adjective.
In a series of more than one adjective before a noun , only the last adjective has a ligature, for example:
Mabait at masunurin g aso .

slides.title: 1 . Noun + noun

paragraphs.text: Ang bata ng babae ay natulog .			The young girl slept.
Ang lolo ko ay matanda ng lalaki .		My grandfather is an old man .
II. OTHER WORD SEQUENCES THAT NEED LIGATURES

slides.title: 11. OTHER WORD SEQUENCES THAT NEED LIGATURES

paragraphs.text: Noun + verb (or verb + noun)
Ang ibon g lumilipad ay binaril . The flying bird was shot.
Ang lumilipad na ibon ay binaril

slides.title: 11. OTHER WORD SEQUENCES THAT NEED LIGATURES

paragraphs.text: 3. Adjective + verb (or verb + adjective)
Pagod na dumating si /ang tatay sa bahay . 			My father arrived home tired .
Dumating na pagod si /ang tatay sa bahay .

slides.title: 11. OTHER WORD SEQUENCES THAT NEED LIGATURES

paragraphs.text: Verb+ adverb (or adverb+ verb)
Kumain g mabilis si Pablo. 						Pablo ate quickly .
Mabilis na kumain si Pablo.
Si Pablo ay kumaing mabilis .

slides.title: 11. OTHER WORD SEQUENCES THAT NEED LIGATURES

paragraphs.text: 5. Noun + adverb ( or adverb + noun)
lwasan ang pag-aaway na matagal .				Avoid the long feud.
lwasan ang matagal na pag-aaway .

slides.title: 11. OTHER WORD SEQUENCES THAT NEED LIGATURES

paragraphs.text: 6. Adjective + adverb (or adverb + adjective)
Mahal na totoo ang relo mo. 			Your watch is truly expensive.
Totoo ng maha l ang relo mo. Napaka -very    Maganda ng - maganda

slides.title: 11. OTHER WORD SEQUENCES THAT NEED LIGATURES

paragraphs.text: 7. Conjunction + adverb
Samantala ng wala , magtiis tayo. While [we have) none , let us be patient.
Sakali ng dumating , paghintayin ang mensahero . If he/she comes, make the messenger wait.
However, the conjunctive kung (which means if) does not need a ligature.
Kung wala pa ako , mauna na kayo. If I am not around yet, you may go 																	ahead.

slides.title: 11. OTHER WORD SEQUENCES THAT NEED LIGATURES

paragraphs.text: Verb + verb
Hinayaan g umalis ang bata.		 		The child was allowed to leave .
Namatay na lumalaban ang sundalo .		The soldier died fighting.

slides.title: EXCEPTIONS TO THIS RULE INCLUDE THE FOLLOWING :

paragraphs.text: a. Verb-verb sequences that result in an adjectival expression
Mamatay -mabuhay ang relo ko.			 	My watch stops periodically .
(literally, dies and lives)
b . Helping verb and main verb sequences
Ayaw kumain ng maysakit .				The sick person does not want to eat.

slides.title: 9. Adverb+ adverb sequences where the adverb is repeated for emphasis

paragraphs.text: Gabi ng -gabi na siya umuwi . He/She came home very late.
Bukas na bukas talaga ay babalik ako .		I shall certainly return tomorrow

slides.title: 11. OTHER WORD SEQUENCES THAT NEED LIGATURES

paragraphs.text: 10. Adjective + adjective sequences where the adjective is repeated to create a superlative
Malinaw na malinaw ang utos niya .			His/her command is very clear .
Mabait na mabait ang guro ko.				My teacher is very kind .

slides.title: l I. Noun + pronoun (or pronoun + noun)

paragraphs.text: Ang bahay na iyan ay akin. That house is mine.
lto ang aking lupa .					 This is my land .

An exception to this sequence is the noun + possessive pronoun ( ko,namin , nila and others) com­bination as the possessive pronoun changes forms when it is placed after nouns. Examples include aklat ko, bahay namin , and lupa nila .
11. OTHER WORD SEQUENCES THAT NEED LIGATURES

slides.title: 12. Pronoun + adjective (or adjective + pronoun)

paragraphs.text: lkaw na marunong ay magsalita . You who are learned should speak.
Ang hangal na ito ay umiyak . This fool is crying.

An exception to the pronoun + adjective or adjective + pronoun sequence is the adjective + nom­inative pronoun sequence . A nominative pronoun such as ka and kayo is a personal pronoun that can be used as the subject of a sentence.
Marunong ka.	You are intelligent (or learned).
Mababait kayo.	You (plural) are kind.
11. OTHER WORD SEQUENCES THAT NEED LIGATURES

slides.title: 13.Verb + pronoun (or pronoun+ verb)

paragraphs.text: Tatawagin g ano ang bata? Tayong kanilang inapi ay natuto .
By what name shall the child be called?	 	We, whom they maltreated , learned.
The verb + pronoun (or pronoun + verb) sequence below is the exception to the list of rules as most combinations of this type do not need ligatures, such as:
Liligaya tayo.			We shall be happy.
Kinuha ko ito .			I took this.
11. OTHER WORD SEQUENCES THAT NEED LIGATURES

slides.title: 14. Pronoun + pronoun

paragraphs.text: Kinuha ninyo yaon g amin.		You took that which is ours .
Tayo ng kanilang inapi ay natuto .		 We, whom they maltreated, learned.
( kanila ng inapi is also an example of a pronoun + verb sequence)
Exceptions to the above sequence include chose in sentences in the subjunctive mood (see first sen­tence) as well as two successive pronouns that form a complete sentence by themselves.
Kung ako ikaw , aalis ako .				If I were you, I will leave.
Kaniya lto .						This is his/hers.
11. OTHER WORD SEQUENCES THAT NEED LIGATURES

slides.title: Observe that, generally, the exceptions in the last four sequences contain either a possessive per­sonal pronoun that comes after a noun such as ko, mo , niya , namin , natin, ninyo nila or a nomi­native personal pronoun that changes form when used in an inverted word order sentence such as ka, kayo, kami, tayo, siya , and sila .

paragraphs.text: Some sequences not mentioned above also do not need a ligature and these will be pointed out later.

Also note that changing the sequence of nouns, adjectives, verbs and adverbs does not change the meaning of the phrases or the position of the ligatures, which still come after the first word. And the resulting sequences still follow the rules for using the ligatures -ng, -g, and na.
bata ng babae or babae n g bata 			 young girl mataba ng lalaki or lalaki ng mataba fat man
ibon g lumilipad or lumilipad na ibon flying bird
pagod na dumating or dumating na pagod	 	arrived tired
kumain g mabilis or mabilis na kumain ate quickly
matagal na pag-aaway or pag-aaway na matagal long feud
mahal na totoo or totoo ng mahal			truly expensive
